sourceNote: All records curated from Wikipedia. Nubra Valley is at 3000–3200m, accessed via Khardung La (5359m). Inner Line Permit required for all foreign nationals and Indian tourists. Road is seasonal (Jun–Sep reliably, partially Oct). All records needs_review.

places.name: Diskit Monastery
places.description: Oldest and largest monastery in Nubra Valley, founded in the 14th century by a disciple of Tsongkhapa. Situated on a ridge 70m above Diskit village. The complex includes prayer halls, a library of manuscripts, and a 32m gold-painted seated Maitreya Buddha statue inaugurated by the Dalai Lama in 2010, visible across the valley. Requires a climb; rewarded with views over the sand dunes and river.

places.name: Hunder Sand Dunes
places.description: Unexpected cold-desert sand dunes at 3100m altitude in the Nubra Valley floor, near Hunder village. The dunes rise against a backdrop of snow-capped peaks. Bactrian (double-humped) camel rides are offered by local operators across the dunes — a rare population of camels descended from ancient Silk Road trade caravans. Best visited at sunrise or sunset for photography.

places.name: Turtuk Village
places.description: Remote Balti village near the Line of Control with Pakistan, 110km from Diskit. Turtuk was part of Pakistan until captured by India in 1971; the Balti-speaking community retains a distinct Central Asian culture and architecture. Terraced apricot and wheat fields, a 15th-century mosque, and narrow carved-wood-balcony lanes. The northernmost tourist-accessible point in Nubra. Full-day excursion from Diskit; requires Inner Line Permit.

places.name: Panamik Hot Springs
places.description: Sulphurous hot springs at Panamik village, the northernmost tourist-accessible point in central Nubra Valley, 45km north of Diskit. The springs emerge near the village at temperatures up to 70°C; a bathing tank is available for visitors. Panamik is also near the Siachen Glacier base area road (restricted beyond). A pleasant 30-minute stop on the road north from Diskit.

places.name: Samtanling Gompa
places.description: Small but active Nyingma school monastery in Sumur village, 20km north of Diskit. Houses Thangka paintings and a statue of Padmasambhava. Considerably quieter than Diskit Monastery; a more contemplative visit. The surrounding Sumur oasis village has apricot orchards. Often passed on the road to Panamik.

places.name: Yarab Tso
places.description: Small sacred high-altitude lake near Diskit town at the floor of the Nubra Valley, considered holy by local Buddhists. Hidden from the main road, accessible via a short walk. The still water mirrors the surrounding bare mountains. Almost entirely unknown to most tourists staying in the Hunder sand-dune area; a quiet hidden alternative within a few kilometres of Diskit.
